title: Regional failure-mode mapping and observability patterns
author: Maya Chen
summary: This document catalogs observed failure modes by region, prescribes a set of reusable observability patterns and dashboard templates, and defines alerting and escalation defaults to keep cross-region inference availability within SLOs. It is intended for platform engineers, SREs, and oncall responders operating Redwood’s hosted and dedicated regions.
body:
Overview:

This page defines a structured approach to mapping regional failure modes (network, capacity, dependency, and control-plane regressions) to specific observability patterns, dashboard templates, and alerting thresholds. It captures:

- canonical metric sets for LLM inference services (runtime, queueing, cache hit-rate)
- dashboard views for triage (region health, tenant impact, degradations)
- per-failure-mode alert rules with severity and oncall routing
- remediation runbook pointers and rollout guidance for dashboards/alerts

Why this matters:

Regional incidents are often similar on surface (elevated latency) but have different root causes and therefore require different mitigations. Standardizing how we observe, alert, and route reduces mean time to detect (MTTD) and mean time to repair (MTTR) and makes cross-region failover decisions more reliable.

Scope and ownership:

- Scope: Hosted API regions, Dedicated region routing tiers, cross-region control plane. This document does NOT cover customer-local Private deployments (see eng-private-deployments).
- Document owner: eng-platform (platform-observability team).
- Oncall owners: eng-sre for region-level escalation; serving-runtime for kernel/interference issues.

Failure-mode taxonomy (high level):

1) Network fabric degradation
   - Symptoms: increasing p95/p99 egress RTT, packet drops on node-level NICs, increased retry rates in edge proxies
   - Typical root causes: provider network congestion, BGP flaps, vSwitch driver regression, peering misconfiguration

2) Local GPU saturation or interference
   - Symptoms: rising per-GPU utilization, kernel retries, higher generation tail-latency only for long-context requests
   - Root causes: noisy neighbor jobs, kernel scheduling bug, degraded cooling causing thermal throttling

3) KV/prefix cache collapse
   - Symptoms: drop in cache hit-rate, sudden increase in model re-computation token/sec, correlated cost-per-token spike
   - Root causes: cache TTL misconfiguration, eviction storms after cache rebuild, rollout that changes key format

4) Load-balancer / routing misconfiguration
   - Symptoms: skewed request distribution across nodes, hotspots, some tenants seeing 502/504 while overall cluster throughput is nominal
   - Root causes: lb hash change, routing policy update, service mesh sidecar failure

5) Control plane or autoscaling failure
   - Symptoms: inability to scale up worker pools, queued requests backpressure, scaling requests stuck in provisioning state
   - Root causes: quota exhaustion, provisioning API errors, image registry latency

Canonical metric sets (recommended for all region dashboards):

- Frontend/edge: requests/sec, 5xx rate, p50/p95/p99 latency (in ms), connection error rate, retries/sec
- Router/LB: per-node qps, route skew (% of traffic per instance), active connections, time-to-first-byte
- Serving runtime: tokens/sec, token-latency p50/p95/p99, batch-size distribution, kv-cache-hit-rate, kv-cache-latency
- GPU & host: GPU_utilization, GPU_memory_free_bytes, kernel-oa-errors, host_cpu_iowait, host_net_dropped_packets
- Queues & throttles: queue_length_by_priority, head_request_age_seconds, backpressure_events
- Cost signals: estimated_token_cost_per_minute, cache-miss_token_count

Dashboard templates (to be installed per-region):

1) Region Overview (one-line health):
   - Top row: SLO health (availability %, error budget burn), region capacity utilization (GPU pools used / total), request qps
   - Middle: latency heatmap (per-model and per-route), cache hit-rate trend, queue depth by tenant tier
   - Bottom: dependency sprocket - external registry / KMS / storage latency and error rates

2) Degradation Triage (for oncall):
   - Focused drill-down for a single symptom (e.g., p99 tail latency increase) with correlated graphs: GPU temp/thermal events, kv-cache hit-rate, router skew, infra network RTT
   - Prebuilt LogQL and trace queries for quick filters (examples below)

3) Tenant Impact Lens:
   - Table of top-25 impacted tenants by error rate, latency regression, and cost impact (estimated tokens lost). Allows quick decision to apply tenant QoS or reroute.

Reusable observability patterns (implementation notes):

- Correlation-first rows: graphs should be paired with correlated dependency signals (e.g., pair p99 latency with kv-cache-hit-rate and gpu_utilization).
- Percentile deltas: show delta from 1h and 24h baseline for p95/p99 to highlight sudden regressions.
- Token-normalized cost: include cost-per-token post-cache to detect hidden cost spikes when cache collapses.
- Error bloom detectors: run a service-level Bloom filter that counts distinct error signatures over 15m to avoid alert storms from identical underlying root-causes.

Alerting defaults and severity mapping:

Table: (as text)

- Sev P0 (SLO at risk or customer-facing outage):
  - Trigger examples: availability below 99.5% for 5m (region-wide), total token throughput drop >30% with error rate >2%
  - Pager: eng-sre primary + serving-runtime secondary
  - Runbook: region outage runbook

- Sev P1 (Degradation that affects SLOs soon):
  - Trigger examples: p99 latency > configured threshold for 10m AND cache-hit-rate drop >20%
  - Pager: oncall platform engineer
  - Runbook: degradation triage runbook

- Sev P2 (Operational anomaly / noise):
  - Trigger examples: single-node GPU thermal events, LB 5xx increase confined to <5% instances
  - Pager: slack alert to #platform-ops, only escalate if persists >30m

Alert rule examples (Prometheus/SigV4 style):

1) Region-wide cache collapse (example):
expr: (sum by(region)(llm_kv_cache_hit_total{job=\"runtime\"}) / sum by(region)(llm_kv_cache_requests_total{job=\"runtime\"})) < 0.60
for: 10m
labels: severity = \"P1\", team = \"platform-observability\"
annotations: summary = \"{{ $labels.region }} KV cache hit-rate below 60% for 10m\"

2) Tail latency escalation (example):
expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by(instance, le)(rate(llm_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m]))) > 2.0
for: 5m
labels: severity = \"P1\"
annotations: summary = \"99th percentile request latency > 2s on {{ $labels.instance }}\"

Runbook pointers (quick links and steps):

- Region outage runbook: steps to suspend non-critical tenants, enable burst capacity, and trigger cross-region failover. Key checks: control-plane API health, autoscaler event log, image-pull errors.
- Cache collapse triage: verify key namespace format, TTLs, recent deployment events; look for coordinated cache warmup traffic causing eviction storms; consider controlled cache-priming sequence.
- GPU interference mitigation: identify noisy tenants via per-tenant batch-size distribution, evict suspect jobs to isolated maintenance pool, and if necessary migrate to dedicated-capacity pool.

Quick diagnostic queries (examples):

- Logs (LogQL):
  {app=\"runtime\", region=\"us-west-2\"} | json | status_code >= 500 | count_over_time(5m)

- Traces (example):
  Service: runtime.v2 -> shows spans for request.router -> scheduler -> kernel.exec -> kv.lookup. Look at kv.lookup latency distribution to rule out cache impact.

Dashboard rollout and change process (how-tos):

1) Authoring: create local dashboard in grafana/editor using the Region Overview template. Add instance selectors and permission groups.
2) Staging: add to the staging region and run through a synthetic traffic scenario (see runbooks/gameday tests). Confirm queries are performant (panel query run-time < 2s).
3) Review: request review from platform-observability and eng-sre (two reviewers).
4) Publish: promote dashboard to production region and register under dashboards catalog with ownership metadata and maintenance window.

Governance and deprecation rules:

- Dashboards must include an explicit owner (team and person) and a maintenance cadence. Dashboards without owner or updates for > 12 months will be flagged for archival.
- Alert rules must have a documented runbook link and a severity rationale. Unjustified P0/P1 rules will be downgraded after review.

Oncall play actions by symptom (cheat-sheet):

1) High p99 latency but normal cache hit-rate
   - Check GPU utilization and kernel error counters
   - If single-node: cordon node and drain; move traffic via lb -> notify infra to investigate noisy neighbor

2) High latency with low cache hit-rate
   - Check recent deployments that touch cache key formats
   - If eviction storm: temporarily increase cache size or add controlled priming job

3) Region 5xx spike with router skew
   - Verify lb config change (last 30m) and routing policies; rollback if necessary
   - Apply targeted tenant QoS to protect SLOs

Post-incident analysis checklist (to include in retrospectives):

- Record timeline of metric inflection points (p95/p99, cache hit-rate, queue depth)
- Map to recent changes (deployments, infra updates, policy changes)
- Identify missing signals that would have reduced MTTD (add instrumentation)
- Update dashboard templates and add new alert rules if needed

Appendix: sample Grafana dashboard JSON snippet (minified example)

{\n  \"meta\": {\"name\": \"region-overview-template\", \"owner\": \"platform-observability\"},\n  \"panels\": [\n    {\"title\": \"Region SLO Health\", \"type\": \"stat\", \"targets\": [\"sum(slo_availability{region=\\\"$region\\\"})\"]},\n    {\"title\": \"KV Cache Hit Rate\", \"type\": \"timeseries\", \"targets\": [\"sum(rate(llm_kv_cache_hit_total[5m])) / sum(rate(llm_kv_cache_requests_total[5m]))\"]}\n  ]\n}

Contacts and escalation matrix:

- Platform-observability (primary): #platform-ops, oncall rotation via PagerDuty (team handle: PD:platform-observability)
- Eng-SRE (escalation): #eng-sre-oncall, PD:eng-sre
- Serving-runtime (secondary): #serving-runtime, PD:serving-runtime

Frequently asked questions (FAQ):

Q: How do we pick p99 thresholds per region?
A: Start with historical 99th percentile baseline over last 90 days and add 25–40% headroom depending on tenant mix. Revisit quarterly and after major model upgrades.

Q: When should we opt for cross-region failover versus burst-capacity?
A: Prefer burst-capacity if the root cause is transient (e.g., capacity pressure) and latency remains within degraded SLO. Failover is preferred for persistent control-plane outages or when data residency and tenant isolation allow it.
